statement: Labor friction is spreading across memory suppliers: the SK hynix union rejected its wage agreement on Aug 25-26, 2026 by 50.08% opposed (7,535 votes) against 49.92% in favor (7,510 votes), a 25-vote margin on 93.81% turnout (15,045 ballots), while the Samsung union ratified its deal in May 2026 by a 73.7% vote on 95.5% turnout (62,616 ballots).
why: Unsettled wage agreements at SK hynix, alongside the Micron Taiwan dispute, raise the odds of disruption at the two largest HBM suppliers.

impact.mechanism: Unresolved labor agreements at HBM makers add a non-technical risk to memory output that feeds GPU module assembly.

evidence.excerpt: SK hynix union REJECTED its wage agreement on Aug 25-26, 2026 by a razor-thin margin
50.08% opposed (7,535 votes) vs 49.92% favored (7,510 votes), a 25-vote margin, with 93.81% turnout (15,045 ballots cast)
